# Positions stated against a confluence

A hydrologic location indexed to a flowline carries that flowline's `id` and a
measure along it. The `id` is specific to one representation of the network:
the NHDPlusV2 `COMID`, the NHDPlusHR `nhdplusid`, the 3DHP `id3dhp`. When the
same location has to hold across representations, the flowline `id` is the
wrong anchor — it does not survive a change of representation, and the 3DHP
flowline `id3dhp` is not stable between 3DHP releases.

A mainstem URI is durable. So is a confluence: the mouth of one identified
mainstem where it enters another. A position stated as a signed distance along
a mainstem from one of its confluences is a record that resolves on any
representation carrying both mainstems — the flowline that realizes it changes,
the distance does not.

This article walks one point on the New Hope River: indexed to NHDPlusV2,
written as kilometers from the Northeast Creek confluence, and resolved on
3DHP. It then cuts a subpath across the Morgan Creek confluence, where the
stretch spans two mainstems and splits at the confluence both mainstems share.

The NHDPlusV2 flowlines and the mainstem-URI lookup ship with hydroloom. The
3DHP sample is fetched from hydrogeofetch; this article is website-only and
does not run on CRAN.

```{r mainstems}
library(hydroloom)
library(sf)

ne <- "https://geoconnex.us/ref/mainstems/2408627"  # Northeast Creek
mc <- "https://geoconnex.us/ref/mainstems/2408909"  # Morgan Creek
nh <- "https://geoconnex.us/ref/mainstems/2408056"  # New Hope River
```

# The two representations

The NHDPlusV2 network is the sample flowlines joined to the 679-row
`comid, mainstem_uri` lookup, with the URI set as `aggregate_id`. The recipe
that ships with hydroloom does the join and casts the flowlines to
`LINESTRING` so `get_subpath()` can cut them.

```{r v2}
source(system.file("extdata", "new_hope_mainstems.R", package = "hydroloom"))

v2 <- add_toids(hy(new_hope_mainstems))
```

The 3DHP network carries the four New Hope mainstems natively in `mainstemid`.
`toid` comes from joining `dnhydrosequence` to `hydrosequence`; `hydrosequence`
is the `topo_sort`.

```{r threedhp}
source(system.file("extdata", "new_hope_3dhp.R", package = "hydrogeofetch"))

d3 <- sf::read_sf(sample_new_hope_3dhp)

m <- match(d3$dnhydrosequence, d3$hydrosequence)
d3$toid <- d3$id3dhp[m]
d3$toid[is.na(d3$toid)] <- ""

d3 <- sf::st_zm(d3)
d3 <- dplyr::transmute(d3,
  id = id3dhp, toid = toid, aggregate_id = mainstemid,
  topo_sort = hydrosequence, length_km = lengthkm, divergence = divergence)

d3hp <- hy(d3)
```

`get_confluences()` finds, on each representation, every place a tributary
mainstem enters another identified mainstem. Each confluence is a hydrolocation
on the receiving mainstem at the outlet of the tributary.

```{r confluences}
v2conf <- get_confluences(v2)
d3conf <- get_confluences(d3hp)

ne_v2 <- v2conf[v2conf$hydro_location_id == ne, ]
ne_d3 <- d3conf[d3conf$hydro_location_id == ne, ]

ne_v2
ne_d3
```

Both representations agree that the Northeast Creek mouth is a hydrolocation on
the New Hope River (`aggregate_id` = `2408056`). The flowline that realizes it
differs — a `COMID` on NHDPlusV2, an `id3dhp` on 3DHP. The confluence is
durable, the flowline is not.

# A point on the New Hope River

Take a point near the Northeast Creek mouth and index it to the New Hope River
on NHDPlusV2. `aggregate_ids` constrains the search to the New Hope River's own
flowlines, so a point near the mouth lands on the receiving river and not on
the tributary. `precision` refines the measure beyond vertex resolution.

```{r index}
point <- sf::st_centroid(sf::st_geometry(v2[v2$id == ne_v2$id, ]))
point_sf <- sf::st_sf(geometry = point)

idx <- index_points_to_lines(v2, point_sf, aggregate_ids = nh, precision = 10)
idx
```

`add_hydro_location_distance()` turns that flowline-and-measure into a signed
distance from the nearest confluence. Passing the Northeast Creek confluence
as the only hydro location writes the distance from it specifically; the sign
is negative because the point sits downstream of the mouth.

```{r distance}
rec <- add_hydro_location_distance(
  data.frame(id = idx$id, id_measure = idx$id_measure), ne_v2, v2)
rec
```

# Resolving on 3DHP

The record — mainstem, confluence, distance — now resolves on 3DHP without
touching the NHDPlusV2 flowline it was made on.
`index_hydro_location_distance()` finds the Northeast Creek confluence on the
3DHP aggregate flowpath axis, adds the distance, and maps the result back to a
3DHP flowline and measure.

```{r resolve}
record <- data.frame(aggregate_id = rec$aggregate_id,
  hydro_location_id = rec$hydro_location_id, distance_km = rec$distance_km)

onto3 <- index_hydro_location_distance(record, ne_d3, d3hp)
onto3
```

`status` is `placed`: the distance fell within the 3DHP flowlines present. A
`past_end` status would mean the arithmetic ran off the end of the flowlines in
hand, with `past_end_km` carrying how far.

The point and the two flowlines that realize it, one per representation:

```{r map}
nh_v2 <- v2[!is.na(v2$aggregate_id) & v2$aggregate_id == nh, ]
nh_d3 <- sf::st_transform(
  d3hp[!is.na(d3hp$aggregate_id) & d3hp$aggregate_id == nh, ], sf::st_crs(v2))

v2_line <- nh_v2[nh_v2$id == idx$id, ]
d3_line <- nh_d3[nh_d3$id == onto3$id, ]

plot(sf::st_geometry(nh_v2), col = "lightblue", lwd = 2, reset = FALSE)
plot(sf::st_geometry(v2_line), add = TRUE, col = "darkblue", lwd = 3)
plot(sf::st_geometry(d3_line), add = TRUE, col = "red", lwd = 3)
plot(sf::st_geometry(point_sf), add = TRUE, pch = 16, col = "black")
```

The point (black) sits on the New Hope River. The NHDPlusV2 flowline that holds
its position (dark blue) and the 3DHP flowline the record resolves to (red)
cover the same stretch of river by different lines.

# One flowline's subpath on 3DHP

A single NHDPlusV2 flowline maps to a span of 3DHP flowlines. Index both of its
ends onto 3DHP with `aggregate_ids`, then `get_subpath()` returns the ordered
3DHP pieces between them. A NHDPlusV2 end can sit a few hundred meters from the
3DHP line, so the search radius is raised to 500 m and `offset` read.
`aggregate_ids` constrains each end to the New Hope River's own flowlines, so
the wider radius cannot pull an end onto a tributary flowline that happens to
fall within it.

```{r subpath}
src <- v2[v2$id == idx$id, ]

e_from <- sf::st_transform(get_node(src, "end"), sf::st_crs(d3hp))
e_to <- sf::st_transform(get_node(src, "start"), sf::st_crs(d3hp))

rad <- units::set_units(500, "m")
i_from <- index_points_to_lines(d3hp, e_from, aggregate_ids = nh, search_radius = rad)
i_to <- index_points_to_lines(d3hp, e_to, aggregate_ids = nh, search_radius = rad)

piece <- get_subpath(
  data.frame(id = i_from$id, id_measure = i_from$id_measure),
  data.frame(id = i_to$id, id_measure = i_to$id_measure), d3hp)

sf::st_drop_geometry(piece)
```

`segment_order` runs 1 at the downstream end upward; `id_from_measure` and
`id_to_measure` cut the end pieces; `length_km` is the piece length. Because
`d3hp` is `sf` and lwgeom is installed, each piece also carries its cut
geometry.

# A stretch across a confluence

A stretch that runs from Morgan Creek down onto the New Hope River spans two
mainstems. `get_subpath()` takes two positions on one mainstem, so the
stretch is two calls split at the Morgan Creek confluence, which lies on both
mainstems.

```{r stretch}
mc_v2 <- v2conf[v2conf$hydro_location_id == mc, ]

on_mc <- v2[!is.na(v2$aggregate_id) & v2$aggregate_id == mc, ]
on_nh <- v2[!is.na(v2$aggregate_id) & v2$aggregate_id == nh, ]

# Morgan Creek, from an upstream point down to its mouth
up_mc <- data.frame(id = on_mc$id[which.max(on_mc$topo_sort)], id_measure = 100)
mouth_mc <- data.frame(id = on_mc$id[which.min(on_mc$topo_sort)], id_measure = 0)
seg_mc <- get_subpath(up_mc, mouth_mc, v2)

# New Hope River, from the confluence downstream
conf_nh <- data.frame(id = mc_v2$id, id_measure = 100)
down_nh <- data.frame(id = on_nh$id[which.min(on_nh$topo_sort)], id_measure = 0)
seg_nh <- get_subpath(conf_nh, down_nh, v2)

head(sf::st_drop_geometry(seg_mc))
head(sf::st_drop_geometry(seg_nh))
```

The two pieces meet at the Morgan Creek mouth. A consumer that wants the whole
stretch as one list concatenates them in flow order, the Morgan Creek pieces
above the New Hope pieces.
